speaker: (the cheesemonger)
text: Twopence the pound. That is the price this morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It was three-halfpence. That was the old price.

speaker: (the cheesemonger)
text: And butter is fourpence, and rising. If you have come for butter, the stall is across. I sell the cheese.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Weigh the pound. Here is the twopence. I am not buying the butter.

speaker: (the cheesemonger)
text: A pound. There. Take it, and look at the beam if you want a quarrel. The beam is not mine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am looking at the penny loaf. It is hardly bigger than a fist.

speaker: (the first prentice)
text: Look at it, then. A fist, and a penny, and the day not fed.

speaker: (the second prentice)
text: The strangers and the forestallers eat white manchet while Englishmen chew bran.

speaker: (the first prentice)
text: Bran, and a loaf you could hide in a glove. That is the market.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The penny is still a penny. The loaf is the thing that changed. I have my cheese. I am not here to mend the beam.

speaker: (the cheesemonger)
text: Then take the cheese and leave the beam to the man who owns it. Twopence, and I have said twopence twice.
